answer: Unclonable chip enrollment binds each agent identity to one physical unclonable-function chip. The registry accepts an identity only after a challenge-response from that chip and revokes any key appearing on two identities. An attacker must buy a separate chip and pay an independent enrollment station per identity; cloning the chip’s secret is physically infeasible.
